content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: abnormal kv-cache eviction + continuous-batcher timeouts in prod (us-west-2). Service= inference-router. Error rate jump +9.6% over baseline. Trigger=eviction_spike. thread_ts=3305006789

emma (oncall): I'm digging in. seeing latency spikes on /v1/generate and an uptick in 503/504 from batcher. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre.

raj (eng-runtime): I see a recent rollout at 14:30 that changed batch config: max_batch_tokens increased from 65536 -> 262144 and max_num_seqs left at 128. That increases memory pressure on KV pools — plausible cause for eviction storms.

kevin (eng-sre): logs look nasty, past minute: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:45:57Z] ERROR evict: kvpool.go:412 eviction: pool_overflow size=10240 target=8192
[2026-03-15T14:46:01Z] WARN batch: batcher.go:289 waiting for max_num_seqs, timed out
[2026-03-15T14:46:02Z] ERROR router: router.go:178 downstream 503 upstream: batcher timeout
```

linda (prodops): Rolling a config hotfix to revert the batch token change. Applying safe limits and reducing max_num_seqs to 64 to reduce concurrent seq memory. Executing now:
```
kubectl set env deploy/continuous-batcher -n prod BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=65536
kubectl set env deploy/continuous-batcher -n prod MAX_NUM_SEQS=64
kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher -n prod
```

emma (oncall): Good. Also activating temporary prefix KV throttling to protect routers: `redis-cli -h kv-throttle SADD throttled_routes inference-router` (will remove after stable).

raj (eng-runtime): After restart we should watch KV eviction rate and batch timeout metrics. If evictions persist we may need to drop quant caches for low-priority customers or route heavy customers to a lower-cost model variant.

alyssa (csm): FYI: AcmeMaps (top tier) reported client errors starting ~14:44 and elevated latency. I'm on a quick call with them, communicated we're performing an urgent rollback and will provide updates every 15m. They asked for ETA on mitigation — gave a conservative 30-45m.

kevin (eng-sre): Early indicators after restart (14:52): eviction rate down ~70%, error rate dropping back but latency still ~300-400ms above baseline for some routes. Continuing to monitor.

emma (oncall): Marking incident as PARTIAL CUSTOMER IMPACT (AcmeMaps + small % of traffic). No data exfiltration concerns. Creating incident doc and will escalate to Sev-2 if we see re-escalation.

raj (eng-runtime): Quick followups for postmortem: 1) why did rollout increase max_batch_tokens without cross-team review 2) add pre-deploy check to reject configs that raise pooled memory beyond threshold 3) add rollout guard to pin max_num_seqs when tokens change 4) tighter alerting on eviction rate jumps.

linda (prodops): Also adding a temporary metric-based autoscale rule to add one more batcher replica if batcher_timeout_rate > 0.5% for 1m. Patch applied.

alyssa (csm): Customer update sent: "We mitigated the issue by rolling back a recent batch config change. Your service should return to normal shortly. We'll follow up with a full incident summary and timeline." They appreciated the proactive updates. :thumbsup:

emma (oncall): Handoff: I'll be on shift for 15 more minutes, then handing to raj for next 4h watch. raj please own the follow-up, ensure incident doc gets a timeline and customer impact numbers (requests, 5xx count, affected regions).

raj (eng-runtime): Taking over monitoring and postmortem lead. I'll collect metrics, attach grafana links and the deploy diff. Please escalate if any regression.

kevin (eng-sre): Quick commands I ran to validate: `curl -sS https://internal-metrics/prod/evictions | jq .rate` -> showing drop from 11.2 -> 3.4. Also validated AcmeMaps error rate at `curl -sS https://slo/acme/errors | jq .5xx_last_10m`.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in progress, partial service restoration observed. Next update in 15m or on significant change. :eyes:
